findings.title: Major AI crawlers are blocked from LinkedIn public pages
findings.evidence: Direct site evidence: https://www.linkedin.com/robots.txt was fetched during this audit. For /, /about-us, and /help/linkedin it returns explicit Disallow: / decisions for GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, and CCBot. OAI-SearchBot is allowed, so this is a broad partial crawler-access restriction rather than a universal block.

suggested_action.summary: If wider AI discovery is a business goal, allow selected retrieval/search user agents to crawl the public, non-member pages that contain LinkedIn’s authoritative product and help information.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: In robots.txt, replace the blanket Disallow: / only for intentionally supported agents with scoped Allow rules for public paths (for example, selected /help/ and /about/ paths). Keep member, profile, feed, search, and authentication paths disallowed; test each intended path with the crawler policy before publishing.
